layout.title: How a water heater works

shows.does: a flame lights under a tank of water and it warms
heat leaks out of the thin walls and the water turns back to cold blue
a thick foam jacket wraps the tank and holds the heat
the water keeps heating and steam pours off the top
a thermostat appears and switches the flame off
the flame lights again and dark fumes spill out under the tank
a flue up the middle carries the hot fumes up and outside
the person opens the tap; cold refill water pours in at the top and mixes into the hot
a dip tube carries the cold water down to the bottom
rust spreads round the bottom of the steel tank
a magnesium rod appears inside and rusts while the tank wall comes clean
a ring traced round the anode rod
the person opens the tap and hot water pours out
the water heater running with the hot tap pouring

layout.why: A gas tank water heater stands cut open in a laundry room with a person waiting at its hot tap; the water and the heat are followed from the flame under the tank, round the jacket, up the flue, in through the dip tube and out the hot tap. The camera opens close on the burner and the tank, frames each added part, and ends on hot water pouring from the tap.

sentences.text: If you light a flame under a tank, you have a water heater.
But heat leaks out, and the water cools.
So you wrap the tank in foam.
But the foam keeps the water heating past scalding.
So a thermostat shuts the flame off at 120 degrees.
But the flame's fumes spill out under the tank.
So a flue carries the hot fumes outside.
But at the hot tap, cold refill water mixes in.
So a dip tube sends the cold water to the bottom.
But that fresh water slowly rusts the steel tank.
So a magnesium rod rusts away instead of the tank.
Open the tap, and hot water pours out.
Congratulations, you built a water heater.

recurring.what: a person waiting at the hot tap
